content.text: All working! The fix was to replace floating point multiplication (`* 100`) with proper integer arithmetic. Instead of multiplying a float by 100 (which causes precision errors), I now parse the string representation of the price directly by splitting on the decimal point and calculating cents as `euros * 100 + cents`. This avoids floating point errors entirely and works for any valid price format.

Fix floating point precision errors when parsing currency amounts

Prices like 39.95 were failing validation because multiplying by 100
produced 3995.0000000000005 instead of 3995. Replace float multiplication
with integer arithmetic: parse the string directly by splitting on the
decimal point and calculating (euros * 100 + cents).

This fixes the issue in parseEuros(), cellCents(), and decimalCommaToCents().
Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
